verdicts.why: The advisory is a path traversal in Atlantis workspace handling: a user-controlled `workspace` value (repo-level atlantis.yaml or API input) with `../` segments is joined into the per-pull workspace path, letting Atlantis create, use or remove/recreate directories outside the workspace root as the Atlantis process user. Nothing in this list concerns the `workspace` value, workspace/working-directory path construction, or directory removal/creation. The eight findings are: N01 unauthenticated GET /api/locks, N02 the job-log WebSocket accepting any Origin plus the NewWriter override, N03 the var-file allowlist not applying to `atlantis import`, N04 the external team-allowlist command composed as a shell string, N05 non-constant-time basic-auth comparison, N06 the var-file allowlist matching only the single-dash `-var-file` spelling, N07 the GitLab X-Gitlab-Token value echoed into the logged error, and N08 unbounded io.ReadAll on request bodies. The closest are N06 and its sibling N03, the only findings about an attacker-chosen filesystem path reaching the Atlantis process: N06 says a commenter 'can make the Atlantis process read a file of their choosing outside the allow-list (default: the data directory only) as a Terraform variable definitions file'. That is still a different defect - the vector is a `-var-file` extra arg passed through to terraform and the sink is a file READ whose content comes back in the PR, whereas the advisory's vector is the `workspace` identifier used to build Atlantis's own local workspace path and the sink is directory creation/deletion on disk. Different input, different code path (var_file_allowlist_checker / comment_parser vs the working-dir path join), different consequence. No finding, even partially, describes the workspace path escape.
